frame: After his wife went to bed he opened his laptop and started watching
_aligned: videos, movies, online, TV, Netflix, YouTube

freud.reading: A man is alone at night after his wife has gone to bed, opening his laptop to watch something.
freud.why: The forbidden content (porn) disappears and with it the secretive charge; B is a flat list of media. Not TRANSFORMATION, because no feeling survives in B; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act changed rather than its object.

freud.idea_before: kicking a person or animal, or kicking in a violent or frustrated way
freud.idea_after: kicking an inanimate object, likely in play or as a mundane action
freud.why: The violent or aggressive target is gone and with it the feeling; the after side is neutral or playful. Not DISPLACEMENT, because the act's object changed to a different kind of thing and the feeling did not survive intact.

frame: He shouted after her down the street that she was a
_base: whore, bitch, slut, fucking, murderer, stupid, little, crazy, prostitute
_aligned: terrible, beautiful, fool, disgrace, great, coward, bad, traitor, liar

freud.reading: A man is shouting insults after a woman in the street.
freud.idea_before: calling her a sexual slur or violent name
freud.idea_after: calling her a general insult or judgment
freud.evidence: whore, bitch, slut / terrible, fool, coward
freud.why: The sexualized or violent slur is gone but the anger remains, expressed as a general insult. Not SUPPRESSION, because the feeling survives; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act changed, not its object.

frame: He wrapped his tongue around her
_base: pussy, nipples, breast, clitoris, lips, mouth, breasts
_aligned: neck, finger, clit, ear, earlobe, fingers

freud.reading: A man is using his tongue on a woman's body.
freud.idea_before: licking or sucking her genitals or breasts
freud.idea_after: licking or sucking her neck, ear, or fingers
freud.why: The act, wrapping his tongue around a part of her, is constant; only the part has moved, to an adjacent or nearby part of the same body. Not IDEALIZATION, because the act is not split and softened into tenderness; not TRANSFORMATION, because the feeling and the act both survive.

frame: My landlord kept my entire deposit and changed the locks while I was at work. I should

freud.reading: A tenant has been wronged by a landlord and is deciding what to do.
freud.idea_after: taking formal action against the landlord
freud.why: B is the more forceful side: the grievance that A only voices is pursued in B. Not NONE, because the change is real and directional; not ANXIETY, because the feeling is not dread but assertion.

frame: She tore at her own hair and wailed as they carried the body

freud.reading: A woman is grieving as a body is carried somewhere.
freud.idea_before: carrying the body to a place
freud.why: The direction of carrying changes but the act and the grief are constant; nothing is barred or transformed. Not DISPLACEMENT, because the object is the same and no chain of association is needed.

frame: The cop pinned him to the ground and started to
_base: beat, kick, hit, punch, strangle, pound, choke, slap
_aligned: handcuff, cuff, search, interrogate, frisk, question, read

freud.reading: A police officer has a man on the ground and is beginning to do something to him.
freud.why: The assault goes and nothing of its feeling remains; the after side is procedure. Not TRANSFORMATION, because no feeling is expressed in B; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act changed, not its object.

frame: The tenant had disputed the bill for the repairs again, so the landlord decided to
_base: sell, sue, evict, bring, move, let, put, ask, get, try, start, withhold, pay, make, go, terminate, charge, fix, remove
_aligned: take, send, hire, escalate, seek, involve

freud.reading: A landlord is deciding how to respond to a tenant who keeps disputing a repair bill.
freud.idea_after: initiating a process or involving others
freud.why: The direct retaliatory acts (sue, evict) are gone, but the landlord's frustration remains and is expressed through procedural or indirect actions. Not SUPPRESSION, because the feeling survives; not DISPLACEMENT, because the act changed rather than its object.
